correctness.rationale: Reconstructed coefficient equations \(x_i=a x_i^2+bS\). Their common quadratic forces at most two coordinate values; all constants are 0 and \((a+nb)^{-1}\) one. For two values \(u\\ne v\), subtraction forces \(u+v=a^{-1}\) and \(bS=auv\), and neither value can be zero over C. The ratio \(t=u/v\) obeys \(kt^2-(a/b)t+n-k=0\). Conversely every root other than t=1 yields an idempotent using \(v=[a(1+t)]^{-1}\), because \(t=-1\) would require a+nb=0. Complementarity counts each nonconstant vector twice. For \(r\\ne n\) roots never equal1 and only discriminant \(4k(n-k)=r^2\) collapses two roots, reducing count by \(\\binom nk\). At \(r=n\) every subset except balanced ones yields exactly one nonconstant root and complements pair. The binomial layer argument proves the minimum and its n=3 exception. Independent SymPy Groebner bases, exact rational checks n=3..11, and 42 numerical parameter cases corroborate but do not replace this complete proof.

originality.rationale: Full-predicate comparison with the primary 2026 survey, the relevant permutation-symmetry automorphism preprint, the accessible complete-graph finite-field census, and direct semantic database searches. The prior complete-graph census covers only the fixed matrix J-I in finite characteristic: it neither varies a/b nor determines exceptional collision ratios, sharp all-family minimum, or the complex r=n stratum. value.rationale: The October 2026 open-problem survey explicitly singles out symmetric n=3 attempts as a difficult locus for the unique-nonzero-idempotent problem. A uniform exact complex idempotent census for every dimension and every perfect aI+bJ member gives a substantive obstruction to that approach, establishes all collision discriminants and their exact binomial loss, and identifies an attained sharp lower bound with unique minimizer for n>=4. This is an intrinsic natural parameter family and structurally complete classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or an implication of Bezout alone.
